articles.title: Arteta sets Arsenal 100-point Premier League target to emulate Manchester City
articles.summary: ‘It’s only been done once and that’s what we want’ Arteta not being drawn on City’s financial charges. Mikel Arteta has set Arsenal the ­target of emulating Manchester City by becoming only the second team in Premier League history to record 100 points in a season.
body: Arteta was an assistant for Pep Guardiola’s side when they achieved the landmark in the 2017-18 campaign, beating second-placed Manchester United by 19 points. City head to the Emirates Stadium on Sunday already trailing Arsenal by six points after just 11 games, with Enzo Maresca’s side having failed to win any of their four previous league matches.

Arsenal drew against Newcastle last week and have only dropped points in one other game so far: a 3-0 defeat at Brighton in September. But Arteta said that his team will have to be exceptional if they are to match City’s record of only two defeats and four draws across the whole season.

“We haven’t hit the level yet that they did and I was there when we did 100 points,” he said. “That’s the level that is unprecedented and every record was beaten. That’s what we have to aim for because that’s what I expect that all the clubs and all the squads with the capacity they have in this league are going to aim for this season or the next few seasons.”

articles.title: No Rodgers, no problem! Steelers shock Broncos after dramatic week
articles.summary: It had been a week clouded by Aaron Rodgers and his explosive claims regarding head coach Mike McCarthy, but the Pittsburgh Steelers swatted at the storm to claim a shock 27-5 win over the Super Bowl-contending Denver Broncos on Black Friday.
body: Broncos quarterback Bo Nix endured a miserable afternoon as he surrendered two interceptions and a lost fumble that resulted in two defensive touchdowns for the Steelers.

Denver trailed 24-5 after a dire first half in which they were limited to just 58 yards of offense, becoming just the third team since 1991 to post fewer than 60 yards while conceding two defensive touchdowns over the first two quarters of a game.

TJ Watt scored with an end zone fumble recovery, Jalen Ramsey returned a Nix interception to the house and D.K. Metcalf recorded a touchdown catch before appearing to celebrate by holding up eight fingers in an apparent support of Rodgers.
The Broncos looked anything but a contender as they slumped to 8-3, while the Steelers distanced themselves from a reflection of turmoil to improve to 7-4 in their push for the playoffs.

articles.title: ‘My Tottenham was born’: De Zerbi harks back to opening defeat for Sunderland return
articles.summary: Spurs head coach intends to draw on last season’s trauma. Italian praises club after Williams-Barnett signs contract. Tottenham’s trip to Sunderland takes Roberto De Zerbi back to the start.
body: The result left Spurs in the bottom three, two points below West Ham, and De Zerbi has not forgotten the reaction in the dressing room after the final whistle. Survival was secured on the final day of last season but he is taking nothing for granted after a promising run of form.

De Zerbi, whose side are six points off the top four after four wins in their last five games, remembers the mood seven months ago and plans to motivate his players before Sunday’s return to Sunderland by showing them footage of their devastation after their previous trip to the Stadium of Light.

“I am thinking of showing this video from the end of the game to the players tomorrow evening,” the manager said. “I want to start my meeting by speaking about that emotion on that day because I don’t want us to forget this moment. It is the key for my Tottenham. Maybe in the future with another coach this will change but my Tottenham was born that day.

articles.title: Spygate tensions erupt at Southampton after Finn Azaz’s cry-baby celebration riles Boro
articles.summary: When asked whether he had any regrets about running the length of the pitch to goad the Middlesbrough supporters he used to call his own with a mock crying celebration, Finn Azaz was unequivocal. “None whatsoever,” said the Southampton playmaker.
body: Southampton, and their manager Tonda Eckert, long ago admitted their Spygate crime. Based on the behaviour of many connected to the south-coast club – their manager a notable exception – they have embraced it. The sense of aggrievement that it cost them the chance of promotion last season remains.

So when the former Boro player Azaz sealed victory in a most heated of contests – the first time these two clubs had met since the scandal – adding a second goal to Ryan Manning’s opener, it was like a champagne cork had been unpopped. “They sang about my family home and away last season so I was just waiting for my moment to get one back,” said Azaz.

It was an astonishing end to a new rivalry that will doubtless only grow given the continued brazen conduct of the guilty party. In the buildup to the match, there had been a public desire from both managers to move on from the events of last May: the intern caught snooping on Middlesbrough training, Southampton’s subsequent expulsion from the Championship playoff final despite claiming victory on the pitch, and the five-month saga spent meting out full punishments.

articles.title: Price out in Players Championship Finals first round in night of upsets
articles.summary: Three of darts' biggest names were subject to shock upsets in the Players Championship Finals as Grand Slam champion Gerwyn Price, World No 2 Gian Van Veen, and No 1 seed Wessel Nijman were all knocked out in the first round at Minehead.
body: Price was beaten by 6-4 Sebastian Bialecki - the first time the Pole had beaten the Welshman in his career - while Jeffery de Graaf won two legs on the bounce to consign van Veen to defeat by the same scoreline.
Nijman was upset by 20-year-old Henry Coates despite posting an average of 110 - the second-highest average in Players Championship Finals history.

World No 4 Luke Humphries, meanwhile, battled through his recurring back injury to secure a routine 6-3 victory against Darryl Pilgrim, while Michael van Gerwen withstood Connor Scutt to secure safe passage with a 6-3 first-round win of his own.

Beau Greaves also progressed to the second round with a scrappy 6-3 victory against former Lakeside champion Christian Kist despite a mediocre average of 89.64, and will face Rob Owen in the next round.

articles.title: 'You're not welcome here' - Chelsea fans turn on Fofana
articles.summary: Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana is booed by his own fans during the Premier League defeat at Nottingham Forest after a controversial interview.
body: Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana was subjected to repeated boos and told "you're not welcome here" by his own fans during Friday's Premier League defeat by Nottingham Forest.
The jeers aimed at the 25-year-old were heard every time he touched the ball and came after an unauthorised interview with French YouTuber Zach Nani was released.
In that controversial two-hour conversation, Fofana also appeared to joke about missing his penalty during last month's Carabao Cup shootout defeat by Liverpool.
Manager Xabi Alonso said the French centre-back had apologised and "it won't be repeated".

articles.title: 'A bit strange' - Leclerc seeking outlier to catch Mercedes in Qatar
articles.summary: Charles Leclerc believes an “outlier” has given Mercedes a “massive” advantage at the Qatar Grand Prix, after Kimi Antonelli and George Russell dominated Friday’s practice sessions.
body: Mercedes were nearly half a second quicker than the rest of the field at the Lusail International Circuit as Antonelli topped both sessions from Russell.

Their four-tenths advantage over closest challenger Lando Norris in second practice could have been even greater, with neither Antonelli nor Russell completing a full low-fuel lap on the soft tyres. It was an ominous sign for the rest of the field ahead of Saturday's qualifying, which gets under way at 6pm, with coverage live on Sky Sports F1 from 5.15pm.

Mercedes' dominance was similar to their pace advantage earlier in the season but the second half of 2026 has largely been very close between F1's top four teams - Mercedes, Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren.
Ferrari were over one second behind Antonelli on a dismal Friday as Leclerc spun in second practice and Lewis Hamilton suffered an engine problem which brought his Ferrari to a halt.

articles.title: Detroit Tigers’ Puzzling Beau Brieske Roster Move Suddenly Makes Sense
articles.summary: When the Detroit Tigers designated right-handed pitcher Beau Brieske for assignment on Friday afternoon, the move raised an interesting question. Why would the Tigers tender Brieske a contract for the 2027 season only to remove him from their 40-man roster a few days later?
body: As it turns out, there may be a strategic reason behind the seemingly contradictory decisions. According to MLive Tigers beat reporter Evan Woodbery, the move could actually increase Detroit’s chances of keeping Brieske in the organization.

The Tigers officially announced one-year contracts with Luis Gil and Ha-Seong Kim on Friday, designating Brieske and infielder Tsung-Che Cheng for assignment to accommodate the additions. However, Woodbery pointed out that Detroit previously used a similar strategy with outfielder Akil Baddoo.
“Why DFA Brieske a few days after tendering him a contract for 2027?” Woodbery wrote on X.

“Similar to what they did with Akil Baddoo a couple years ago: The tender could dissuade teams from claiming Brieske off waivers. If he goes unclaimed, he’ll be outrighted and become a well-paid Mud Hen.”
